builder_plan.scenario: Your coding assistant makes changes that still need substantial repair before merging.
builder_plan.change: Try the technique on held-out issues from a repository with reliable tests.
builder_plan.baseline: The same coding agent, repository snapshot, tools, and token budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct patches, regression failures, human repair time, and total cost per accepted change.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: How Should Agents See Code? Rethinking Code Representations for Agentic Software Engineering
summary: The technique replaces raw-file and lexical-search repository access with queryable repository maps (ASTs, call graphs, module dependencies, documentation-enriched search, or hybrids) that agents consult during tasks. It costs additional latency on some benchmarks, increased token usage on test-generation tasks, and engineering effort to build and maintain the repository indexes. Benefits are task-dependent: gains are strongest for localization bottlenecks and narrow or vanish when patch or test authoring is the decisive step.
rationale: The token savings and localization gains are achievable with third-party APIs and modest tooling, but benefits vary by task type so the reader should validate on their own workloads before adopting broadly.
technique: Map-based code representations for coding agents

claims.statement: The technique replaces raw-file and lexical-search repository access with queryable repository maps (ASTs, call graphs, module dependencies, documentation-enriched search, or hybrids) that agents consult during tasks. It costs additional latency on some benchmarks, increased token usage on test-generation tasks, and engineering effort to build and maintain the repository indexes. Benefits are task-dependent: gains are strongest for localization bottlenecks and narrow or vanish when patch or test authoring is the decisive step.

On LinuxFLBench, all five workflows improve recall@10 (0.757-0.829 vs. 0.717 baseline) and reduce token usage by 25-39%; on SWE-bench Pro, token usage drops 17-26% with resolution near baseline (44.3-50.6% vs. 49.0%).
